title: Outliers and bounded rank perturbation for non-Hermitian random band matrices: a matrix-unit block computation for the model parameters
author: Yi HAN
work: Outliers and bounded rank perturbation for non-Hermitian random band matrices
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma (source0.tex lines 1089--1130, source label lem:block-parameter), a matrix-unit block computation: for a random matrix written as a sum of mutually independent zero-mean blocks of distinct matrix units with bounded coefficients, bounded block covariance and pseudo-covariance, and doubly stochastic normalisation, the article's four model parameters satisfy sigma(X) = 1, sigma_*(X) <= L^{1/2} kappa_N, v(X) <= L^{1/2} kappa_N and tilde v(X) <= L^{1/4} kappa_N^{1/2}, and the block supremum bound R(X) is at most the largest essential supremum of the blocks, with the sharper matching-supported form stated in the lemma; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1133--1192 (one adjacent proof environment of 60 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span and uses nothing outside the statement. It rewrites the quadratic form of the matrix against a pair of unit vectors as a linear combination of the block coefficients, bounds its second moment through the block covariance and pseudo-covariance hypotheses, uses the distinctness of the matrix units and the boundedness of the coefficients to reduce the resulting sum to kappa_N squared times the squared norm product, obtains the lower spectral parameter bound, repeats the same computation for the Hilbert-Schmidt pairing to bound the parameter v, combines v with the normalisation to control tilde v, and finally reads off the block supremum bound from the definition of R as the largest essential supremum among the independent blocks. The lemma is the technical input through which the article's general model assumptions are verified for its band-matrix ensembles, and its proof is a complete research-level parameter computation. H2: a research-level random-matrix lemma whose proof combines a second-moment computation under block independence, a matrix-unit distinctness count, a Hilbert-Schmidt pairing argument and a doubly stochastic normalisation; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
